Airbots is one proactive assistant across your whole stack, not one bot per job. You pick which tools to connect, from Google Workspace to Slack and Salesforce. results.title: Why Airbots Puts an AI Chief of Staff in Your Messages
results.content:
## What Airbots is

Airbots is a personal assistant that is always on, keeping track of every deal so you can close as much revenue as possible. The team describes it as a know-it-all chief of staff, occasionally a little annoying, that makes you perform at your best. It learns you, your sales process and your customers, and it will push you when that is what it takes to close.

## Why WhatsApp and iMessage

Communicating and executing are moving into the same place. You either talk to your human colleagues or you talk to your AI, and both happen in messaging apps. [...] ## Catching deals before they slip

Most AI tools won’t notice that a deal is about to slip, because they aren’t looking for the right signals. Airbots watches continuously and flags a deal as soon as the risk appears.

It also knows when to stay quiet. Rather than sending a notification for every small issue on every small deal, it focuses on your most important deals and speaks up when the biggest risks emerge.

## Doing the work, not only flagging it

If you don’t act, Airbots can act for you. It might loop in an additional stakeholder or prepare a re-engagement email, and tell you plainly: here is the email, ready to send, and if I don’t hear from you, I’ll send it. [...] ## Starting with the person

Airbots turns this around. It starts with how much a person can realistically take in and works backwards from there. Everything happens in a single thread, which means the experience can be curated: short messages, only the most critical items, such as the three things you should do this morning to hit your number.

This is the real shift. AI is the tool, and the human is the design brief.
